from_idea: Akien 2026-08-19, resolving open-a-saturated-match-rate-cannot-show-efficacy: sieves measure deterministically, LLM periodic review of feedback adjusts the parameters
intention: Scheduled probes fire LLM prompts to Hex for periodic inspection of gate feedback. The sieve stays deterministic Python; what changes is what it is calibrated against. The LLM reviews accumulated feedback and proposes parameter adjustments.
why: A sieve that measures at 100% match rate cannot show efficacy — it agrees with everything. The feedback the sieve collects is where efficacy hides, but nobody reads it. Hex reviewing the feedback on a schedule closes the loop: the sieve measures, the feedback accumulates, the LLM reads the feedback, the parameters adjust, the sieve measures differently.
traces_to: Law 4 — a gate whose parameters never adjust from evidence is policy wearing physics' clothes. The adjustment loop is what makes it physics.
learns-its-gates founding intention — the system learns its gates from evidence; a hand-set constant in a gate is a learned value stranded in a human's head.
sieves-measure-not-judge — the sieve stays deterministic Python; the LLM reviews feedback PERIODICALLY, never in the measurement path.
Law 1 — Hex reading accumulated feedback is compiling the observation once; a human re-reading the same feedback each session is re-deriving.
gates: THREE things must work: (1) a gate collects feedback in a shape Hex can read — structured JSON, not prose, carrying the sieve's input, its output, and the gate owner's disposition if any; (2) a scheduled probe fires an LLM prompt to Hex with the accumulated feedback and receives a proposed parameter adjustment; (3) the adjustment lands THROUGH the gate's own door (Law 6 — the gate owner approves or rejects). The gate owner is the component, not the LLM — Hex proposes, the gate's physics accepts or refuses.
falsifier: RED if: (1) the LLM is in the measurement path — a sieve that calls an LLM to DECIDE is not deterministic and violates sieves-measure-not-judge; (2) the adjustment bypasses the gate owner's approval — the gate's own door is the only write path (Law 6); (3) the schedule is a polling loop or a daemon rather than a probe fired by an event that already fires (shrinking-footprint: event not poll); (4) the feedback shape is not parseable by a local LLM — Hex is the M1 Studio box, not CC, and the feedback must be structured enough for a smaller model to read; (5) a parameter adjustment that makes the sieve WORSE has no rollback path — the adjustment must be reversible by the same door it entered through.
horizon: After the feedback tool's route is built (cairn/tools/feedback) and at least one gate collects structured feedback. There is no point adjusting parameters nobody collects yet. The feedback tool is upstream; this ticket is the CONSUMER of what it produces.
dependencies: cairn/tools/feedback — the tool that owns the feedback route and the shape of a declared route. This ticket consumes what it produces.
inference_domain — the sole path to Hex (the M1 Studio inference box). The LLM prompt goes through this domain and no other.
A gate that already collects data in a structured shape — at least one sieve must be producing feedback records before this can fire against real data.
sub_tickets_owed: a gate collects feedback in a shape the LLM can read
a scheduled probe fires an LLM prompt to Hex with accumulated feedback
Hex proposes parameter adjustments and the gate owner approves or rejects
the adjustment lands through the gate's own door (Law 6)
distinctions_recorded: The sieve is DETERMINISTIC PYTHON ONLY. The LLM is in the parameter-adjustment loop, never in the measurement path.
This is the learns-its-gates founding intention made concrete for one gate shape.
Hex is the inference target (the M1 Studio box), not CC. CC is too expensive for periodic review.
The schedule fires from a probe — an event that already fires (the heartbeat, or a feedback-count threshold) — never a new timer or daemon.

chart_notes.orient: The feedback accumulates beside the gate that produces it, in structured JSON. The prompt to Hex carries the accumulated records and the current parameter values. inference_domain is the sole path to Hex.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: the LLM in the measurement path (the sieve stays deterministic Python); a new daemon or timer (the probe fires from an existing event); CC as the reviewer (Hex is cheaper and local). IN: the adjustment loop, the feedback shape, the gate owner's approval door.
chart_notes.validate: A parameter adjustment proposed by Hex and accepted by the gate owner changes the sieve's output on the same input. The before/after is measurable: same input, different disposition, and the feedback that motivated the change is named in the adjustment record.

filed_edges: The same feedback-review pattern applies to EVERY gate with parameters, not just sieves. This ticket builds it for one shape; the pattern transfers on the shape of the gate, not the identity of the sieve.
The adjustment record is itself a measurement (Law 10) and belongs in the gate's own history — not in a separate store.

watchme.trigger: a scheduled LLM inspection completes and produces feedback on gate calibration
watchme.enough: three inspection cycles where the feedback led to a parameter adjustment, or Akien rules the initial calibration stable
watchme.carrier: the before/after gate parameter values and the feedback that prompted the change
watchme.consumer: Akien at triage — the inspection cycle must demonstrably tune the gates, not merely confirm them
